test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Oct 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is NOT an instrument of **the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a tax on goods and services. It is an indirect tax that was implemented to replace a variety of other indirect taxes such as **VAT, service tax, purchase tax, excise duty,** and so on.
 
• GST is a tax applied in India on the supply of certain goods and services. It is a single tax that applies throughout India.
 
• The fundamental goal of this taxing scheme, which is applicable throughout India, is to reduce the cascading effect of other indirect taxes.
 
• **India **implemented the Goods and Services Tax on **July 1, 2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **uses a liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) to allow banks to borrow money through repurchase agreements (repos) or make loans to the RBI through reverse repo agreements.
 
• **The cash reserve ratio (CRR)** is the amount of liquid cash a bank must keep as a percentage of total deposits.
 
• **The repo rate** is the rate at which a country's central bank (in India, the Reserve Bank of India) loans money to commercial banks in the event of a cash shortage.
